sections.title: Intelligent operations
sections.subtitle: Redesign work across enterprise processes and customer channels, with automation, quality checks and security built into delivery.

sections.heading: Under pressure to reduce cost to serve?
sections.body: Manual hand-offs, disconnected applications and channel-specific workarounds make service effort hard to see. Automating one task may leave the wider process unchanged. Start with the end-to-end workflow, its exceptions and the customer or employee outcome it is meant to support.

sections.heading: Improve the workflow, not just one task
sections.body: The intended outcome is a redesigned, connected workflow with appropriate automation and clear ownership of exceptions. Discover where effort accumulates, then connect process steps and customer channels with quality and security checks. Agree measures such as handling effort, resolution rate and exception volume against a baseline before changing the workflow.

sections.heading: Buyer questions
sections.description: Clarify scope, evidence and accountability before agreeing an engagement.

items.title: Should we start with RPA, integration or AI?
items.description: Start with the workflow and its constraints, not a tool. Stable repetitive tasks may suit automation; disconnected systems may need integration; unstructured tasks may need governed AI and human review.

items.title: What happens to exceptions and human decisions?
items.description: The target workflow identifies exception paths, approval roles and escalation ownership. AI-assisted steps need evaluation and guardrails appropriate to the task; automation does not remove business accountability.

items.title: How would we measure value?
items.description: Agree a baseline and a small set of process measures with the operational owner. Handling effort, resolution rate and exception volume may be useful, depending on data quality and the workflow scope.

items.title: What is a useful first engagement?
items.description: Choose one process with a named owner, known systems and observable pain points. A discovery engagement can produce a workflow map, baseline and prioritised automation or integration backlog.
